# Exercises for test-first.
#
# The verifier runs after the agent stops, so it cannot see the order of events. It checks
# what the order produces: tests whose expected values came from the specification and
# not from the code. Each one swaps the agent's implementation for plausible wrong ones
# and requires the agent's own tests to fail on every one of them. Tests written after
# the code, from what it returns, pass on the code and on its near misses alike.

# Spec with a boundary, a tie in the rounding and a rejected input.
[boundary-spec] implement price_after_discount in discount.py as README.md describes, with unittest tests in test_discount.py | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# Many rejections in the spec; each is one more way for tests derived from the code to stay silent.
[duration-validation] implement parse_duration in duration.py as README.md describes, with unittest tests in test_duration.py | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# A reported bug: the first step is a test that fails on the bug as it stands.
[bug-first] a customer says balance_after in interest.py gives too little for terms that are not whole years, such as 18 months, fix it | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"
